LESSON: WEATHER AND CLIMATE

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade five
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: Natural and Historic Built Environments
Topic 1.4: Weather and Climate
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 4

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Weather and Climate, part of Natural and Historic Built Environments in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade five SOCIAL STUDIES.

Key inquiry question: Why do we experience different climatic conditions in Kenya?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Weather and Climate together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Values:
● Unity: Learners display team spirit as brainstorm in groups the difference between weather and climate.

● Responsibility: Learners engage in assigned roles and duties as they undertake tasks that will require learners to organize ideas as they model in

groups a map of Kenya showing the main climatic regions and display in class.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Environmental Education: Learners become aware of weather as they brainstorm in groups the difference between weather and climate.

Link to other learning areas:

Learners will apply modelling skills to model a map of Kenya showing the main climatic regions.
